question: In tennis, what is a 'love' score?

options.text: The score when the game is tied
The highest possible score in a game
The score when a player has zero points
The score when a player wins the first point in a game

solution:
The correct answer is __**The score when a player has zero points**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Love** in tennis refers to a score of **zero points**.
 
• The term **"love"** is believed to come from the French word **"l'oeuf"**, meaning "egg," symbolizing zero.
 
• It is used at the start of the game and when a player has not yet scored any points.
 
• Tennis scoring progresses from love (zero) to 15, 30, 40, and game point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Scoring System**: Tennis scoring is unique and progresses in a sequence: 0 (love), 15, 30, 40, and game point.
 
• **Deuce**: When both players have a score of 40, it's called a deuce. A player needs to win by two consecutive points to win the game from deuce.
 
• **Advantage**: After deuce, the player who wins the next point has the advantage. If they win the next point, they win the game; if they lose it, the score returns to deuce.
 
• **Set**: A set is won by the first player to win six games with at least a two-game lead.
 
• **Match**: Matches are typically played best of three or five sets, depending on the tournament rules.
